elements.element: Customer is not required to use Vendor as its sole or exclusive provider of hosted analytics services.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly makes Vendor “a non-exclusive provider.”

elements.element: Customer is not restricted from obtaining the same or similar hosted analytics services from alternative providers.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits Customer to procure the same or similar services from any third party at any time.

elements.element: If exclusivity applies, it is limited to a specifically defined product category.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity applies, so the condition requiring a category limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If exclusivity applies, its duration does not exceed 12 months.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity applies, so the condition requiring a 12-month duration cap is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If exclusivity applies, it ends automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity applies, so the condition requiring this automatic-termination trigger is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If exclusivity applies, it ends automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet applicable delivery dates.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity applies, so the condition requiring this automatic-termination trigger is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The operative language clearly eliminates Customer exclusivity and therefore satisfies the preferred position; the fallback protections are moot because no exclusivity exists. However, the redline unnecessarily deletes “throughout the term,” potentially removing Vendor's separate obligation to remain a provider for the agreement term. A tighter revision would retain that duration language while changing only the exclusive-provider status and confirming Customer's third-party procurement right.
